questions.question: A shop keeps one product in stock. What does an inventory policy for this product specify?
options: How much stock to hold on average, whatever the order timing
When to replenish the stock and how much to order each time
Which demand the shop should expect in each future period
How large an order should be, leaving its timing open

questions.question: A warehouse manager writes down four candidate rules for one item. Which of them is a complete inventory policy?
options: Order 200 units each time the stock falls to 40 units.
Order 200 units, taking about a week for the delivery.
Place an order each time the stock falls to 40 units.
Keep the stock between 40 and 240 units at all times.

questions.question: Demand for an item is steady. A firm switches from small frequent orders to larger orders placed less often. What happens to its stock and its number of orders?
options: Both the average stock and the number of orders fall.
Average stock and the order count both go up together.
Average stock rises, while the number of orders falls.
The stock held is unchanged, as total demand is unchanged.

questions.question: An analyst sets up an optimization model for a firm's stock of one item and then reports an inventory policy. How do the model and the policy relate?
options: The model fixes the allowed decisions and their evaluation; the policy supplies the decisions.
The model and the policy are two names for one and the same set of ordering rules applied over time.
The model forecasts future demand; the policy is the forecast turned into a stock level to keep.
The model lists the costs only; the policy then has to be found by trying it out in practice.

questions.question: In which demand setting must an inventory policy consist of a single stock quantity, chosen before any demand is observed?
options: A constant, known demand rate over a long horizon
Random demand in one selling period, no reorders
Known demand that varies from one period to the next
Random demand, with new orders possible on any day

questions.question: Demand is 18 units per day. The policy is to order 90 units whenever the stock reaches 0; orders arrive immediately, and stock is 0 at the start of day 1. How many orders are placed at the starts of days 1 to 30?
options: 6, at the start and then every 5 days
5, one every 5 days after the start
7, one every 5 days, up to and including day 31
3, one for every 180 units of demand

questions.question: Every Monday a shop places an order large enough to bring its stock of an item up to 80 units; orders arrive immediately. On one Monday the stock is 25 units before ordering. How many units are ordered?
options: 55 units, to bring the stock up to 80
80 units, the level written in the rule
105 units, the level plus current stock
25 units, to replace the stock on hand

questions.question: Known demands in periods 1 to 5 are 20, 35, 15, 30, 25 units. The policy orders in periods 1, 3 and 5, each order covering the demand up to the next order period. How many units are ordered in period 3?
options: 15 units, the demand of period 3 alone
45 units, the demand of periods 3 and 4
70 units, the demand of periods 3 to 5
55 units, the demand of periods 1 and 2

questions.question: Demand is 10 units per day. The policy is to order 100 units whenever the stock falls to 20 units; orders arrive immediately, and stock starts at 120 units. Between which levels does the stock move?
options: Between 0 and 100 units
Between 20 and 100 units
Between 0 and 120 units
Between 20 and 120 units

questions.question: A firm knows its demand for an item in each of the next six months: 30, 50, 20, 60, 40 and 30 units, differing by month, and it may order at the start of any month. Which form of inventory policy fits this demand setting?
options: Order a fixed quantity whenever stock falls to a fixed trigger level, as for a constant rate
Choose one quantity for the whole six months before any demand occurs
Order in selected months, each order covering the known demands up to the next order
Order the average monthly demand, about 38 units, at the start of every month

questions.question: An optimization model is built to choose an inventory policy for one item, and the warehouse can hold at most 500 units of it. Where does this limit belong in the model?
options: In the objective, as a cost to be made as small as possible
Among the decision variables, as a quantity chosen by the model
In a constraint, limiting which ordering decisions are allowed
Nowhere: a policy can simply be checked against it afterwards

questions.question: An optimization model chooses how much to order in each of the next 12 weeks, given forecast weekly demands. Which quantities are the decision variables of this model?
options: The 12 forecast weekly demands
The total demand over the 12 weeks
The stock capacity of the warehouse
The 12 weekly order quantities

questions.question: A bakery decides each morning how many loaves to bake for that day only; demand is random, anywhere between 80 and 120 loaves. Why can no choice of quantity rule out both leftover loaves and unmet demand?
options: Baking exactly the average, 100 loaves, rules out both of these outcomes.
Baking 120 loaves rules out both, since demand can never exceed it.
Any amount under 120 may fall short; any amount over 80 may be left over.
The amount can be revised during the day once demand has been seen.

questions.question: Known demands in periods 1 to 4 are 30, 10, 40, 20 units; orders arrive immediately. Policy X orders each period's demand in that period. Policy Y orders in periods 1 and 3 only, each order covering two periods. How do the two policies compare?
options: Y places 2 fewer orders and carries no stock into later periods.
Y places 2 fewer orders but carries 100 units into later periods.
Y places 2 fewer orders but carries 30 units into later periods.
Y places as many orders as X but orders larger amounts in total.

questions.question: Each Monday a shop orders enough to bring its stock up to 100 units; orders arrive immediately. Stock is 100 at the start of week 1, and the demands in weeks 1, 2, 3 are 30, 45, 25 units. How many units are ordered in total on the Mondays of weeks 2, 3 and 4?
options: 300 units, as 100 units are ordered each Monday
100 units, the demand of the three weeks
45 units, the largest single weekly demand
75 units, the demand of weeks 1 and 2 only

questions.question: Demand is 25 units per day. The policy is to order 250 units whenever the stock reaches 50 units; orders arrive immediately, and stock starts at 300 units. How many days pass between consecutive orders?
options: 12 days, as the 300 units at the start last 12 days
2 days, as the 50 units left at the trigger last 2 days
8 days, as the 200 units above the trigger last 8 days
10 days, as each order of 250 units lasts 10 days

questions.question: A policy for an item states both the order quantity and the ordering period: order 120 units at the start of every 4 weeks. Weekly demand is a steady 40 units. Does this complete policy meet all demand?
options: Yes: a policy that states both quantity and timing is complete.
Yes: the stock left from earlier periods covers any shortfall.
No: a policy must order whenever stock reaches 0, not by the calendar.
No: each 4-week period has 160 units of demand against 120 supplied.

questions.question: Suppose an inventory model for an item with steady demand counts only a fixed charge per order placed, and no cost at all for stock held. Which policy does the model then favour?
options: Ordering as rarely as possible, in large amounts
Ordering exactly each day's demand every day
Ordering in medium amounts at regular times
Any policy, as every policy meets the same demand

questions.question: Demand is 20 units per day for 60 days, and stock is 0 at the start. The policy is to order $Q$ units whenever the stock reaches 0; orders arrive immediately, so the stock never exceeds $Q$. The firm allows at most 10 orders in the 60 days and at most 150 units in stock at any time. Which value of $Q$ satisfies both limits?
options: $Q=100$, with 12 orders and at most 100 units
$Q=160$, with 8 orders and at most 160 units
$Q=60$, with 20 orders and at most 60 units
$Q=125$, with 10 orders and at most 125 units

questions.question: Known demands in periods 1, 2, 3 are 30, 40, 50 units; orders arrive immediately at the start of a period, stock is 0 at the start, and at most 20 units may be carried from one period to the next. What is the smallest possible number of orders?
options: 2, ordering in period 1 for periods 1 and 2
3, since periods 2 and 3 need over 20 each
2, ordering in period 1 and in period 2
1, a single order of 120 units in period 1
